decisions: Voice leaves a card (owner decision, 7 October): in a live voice conversation, an action that needs approval is not run; it leaves an approval card on the dashboard and in chat, and Jarvis says so. Realtime voice auto-approved such calls before.
Voice may keep pressing dashboard buttons (owner decision): granting access, running a workflow, starting an agent or restarting Jarvis by voice stay as they are; recorded as a known path.

Pause holds, Kill stops (owner decision). Pause: nothing new starts or continues; queued and waiting work waits; a scheduled time is skipped and shown; a webhook is told to retry later; approving a card waits for Resume; a run already executing parks at its next step and Resume releases it. Kill: also stops every unfinished run, denies every pending approval and stops tools in flight at their next dispatch checkpoint; Reset starts nothing again.

Approving from chat (owner decision): only a sender on the channel's allowed users list, with the card's 8-character id; with no list, chat can still deny. Main's #851, merged since, also refuses deny from an unlisted sender; integration takes main's stricter rule unless the owner wants deny back.

Defaults: an unanswered chat or background card expires after 24 hours (workflow approvals keep their own lifecycle); community pieces and CODE steps stay opt-in, without per-run approval, but obey Pause and Kill and are audited.
behavior: An approval request records whom it was asked for (role, level, profile). When the approved call runs, the executor judges it again as that agent, the way its gate did, with the approval standing in for the approval it asked for: a deny override, a context rule or a revoked permission added since the card was raised stops it. A request from before records no one and is asked for again.

A card that must be reviewed on screen (browser and desktop actions) is approved on the dashboard only: a chat reply, a toast or a spoken yes is refused and the card stays pending, and the executor refuses an approval from anywhere else.
Two surfaces deciding one request dispatch it once (compare-and-set decision, one execution claim), now tested through the shared decision path.
Approving while Jarvis is paused or stopped is refused, saying so; the card stays pending for Resume. Denying works.
Realtime voice: a call that needs approval leaves a deferred card with the agent's principal and is not run; with no approval channel it is refused; with no primary agent the gate fails closed.

A request_approval the person did not approve (denied, expired or unanswered) governs its category for the rest of the turn, so a later tool call in it needs its own approval. A task cancelled while its card waits withdraws the card. A spoken yes or no decides nothing while more than one card waits.

Pause and Kill below every UI control: tool dispatch refuses at the agent gates (existing) and, on Kill, at every dispatch checkpoint inside a running tool; the workflow worker claims nothing; a job claimed as the pause began goes back untouched; Kill stops every unfinished run and denies every pending approval; triggers start nothing (a scheduled time is recorded as skipped, keyed so it is not run late; a webhook gets 503 with Retry-After; an event source is not polled, so its items wait); timers, approvals and resume URLs wake nothing (a resume URL answers 503); starting a run by hand (dashboard, chat, work item) is refused, saying why; a governed workflow step, a community piece or a CODE step reached while paused parks on a HOLD waitpoint that Resume releases (a resume URL never can); a recorded piece or delegation authorization is not handed out again while paused or stopped.

The emergency controller is the one source of truth: the engine's copy of the state follows every change (it was the boot snapshot, which kept workflows blocked after Resume), a learning accept no longer writes the state back (which could turn a Kill to normal across a restart), and every change is audited.

A governed piece's approval binds a digest of the whole resolved input, connection excluded, alongside the card's projection: a longer body or more recipients than the card could show need a new approval.

Receipts stay distinct: a tool that could not say whether it took effect leaves the request unresolved (unknown, never run again, closed by a person); nothing started is blocked, not failed. Chat replies, the dashboard notification, the tray and the Task complete toast say what the receipt says. Every decision is audited with its surface (click, chat, notification, voice) and every receipt with its outcome.

A config change is validated before it is applied, and a level that is not a number counts for nothing (it used to pass every level check). A learning suggestion can be accepted only if the learner made it.
Work-item runs check the workflow's CODE-step grant, as every other start does.

manual_checks: Not run against a live daemon: no real provider, browser, desktop or voice session is needed for these fixtures (delivery contract). The quick path below names the manual checks for a dev daemon.

quick_verify.manual: On a dev daemon: press Pause with a workflow waiting on a delay that comes due, then Resume (it continues after Resume, not before); press Kill with a run queued and a card pending (the run is stopped and the card denied, each saying why); in a voice session ask for something that needs approval (a card appears on the dashboard and nothing runs); approve a browser-action card from Telegram (refused: approve it on the dashboard).
quick_verify.screenshot: not applicable: no visible UI changes

migration: Additive: column approval_requests.principal and waitpoint type HOLD. A pending request created before this build has no principal; if approved, it is refused when it runs and asked for again.
rollback: Revert the Q-08 commits. The column and the waitpoint type are additive and ignored by older builds. Resume Jarvis before rolling back: a HOLD waitpoint left by a run parked while paused is not released by an older build.
limitations: Voice can still press dashboard buttons that change permissions or start work (owner decision).
Community pieces run with Jarvis's own permissions and can read any saved connection: the Library's opt-in trust model, unchanged.
A delegated agent's allowed calls are checked but not listed as run effects (Q-10).
Approval cards show what will happen, not the raw arguments (dashboard work).
Kill stops a tool at its next dispatch checkpoint: one command already running on a machine finishes; a sub-agent's model loop is not aborted, its tool calls are refused.
An intent grant (request_approval) is recorded as executed.
Opportunity activation has no route of its own; accepted work items start through the run route.
The 24-hour expiry and the Kill and Resume wiring in daemon/index.ts are thin calls into tested functions; the daemon process itself is not started by the tests.
found: An approved request ran under the permissions in force when it was raised: tightening permissions afterwards did not stop it, inline, deferred or after a restart.
Realtime voice auto-approved every call that needed approval except taint-gated ones, and ran ungated with no primary agent.
A click-only review card could be approved from Telegram, Discord or a toast; only voice refused it.

Kill only changed a flag: nothing stopped runs, denied pending approvals or interrupted tools, and the engine's copy of the state was the boot snapshot (workflows stayed blocked after Resume until a restart, and a learning accept could write a Kill back to normal).

Under Pause the workflow worker kept claiming jobs, triggers kept starting runs, timers, approvals and resume URLs kept waking runs, and an approved step reached while paused was refused for good instead of held.
Community pieces and CODE steps never asked the daemon anything, so no Pause or Kill applied to them, and they left no audit row.
A piece approval bound a projection cut twice (512 characters, 25 items, 40 keys, depth 5), so a longer body or more recipients ran under an approval for fewer.
A recorded piece or delegation authorization was handed out again before any check, including during an emergency.
A tool that could not say whether it took effect was recorded as failed; blocked runs, intent grants and authorizations read as executed in replies, toasts and the tray.

A denied request_approval did not stop the same action through a tool the level allowed; a cancelled task's card stayed approvable; cards never expired; a spoken yes approved the newest card across all agents.
POST /api/authority/config accepted a non-number level, which passed every level check; learning accept added an always-allow override for any action.
Work-item runs skipped the CODE-step grant check.
